statusText: Green. The weekend CME halt continues with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail sits at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.

headline: Nasdaq-100: hawkish September repricing still untested behind the weekend halt; tail risk holds the low-band floor into the Sunday reopen
body: This assessment is made inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The verified anchor remains Friday's close: NDX 29,433.43, down 0.70%, settling in the lower third of a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range, with VIX 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 day range. The dominant open question is policy pricing rather than price structure. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks lifted September rate-hike odds from roughly 35% to about 60% on CME pricing, and the 2-year yield rose 11 basis points to 4.34%, its highest in a month. H.15 constant-maturity yields for 27 August stand at 4.20, 4.38, 4.67 and 5.19 percent for 2Y, 5Y, 10Y and 30Y, and Friday's move added a bear-flattening shape more consistent with policy repricing than with a growth shock. Cross-asset alignment is only partial: sharply higher short-end yields against a calm VIX and a soft crude tape, with WTI at 83.44 dollars and Brent at 88.29 dollars after a weekly decline of roughly 4 percent as the Iran confrontation was read as a sanctions and economic dispute rather than an imminent physical supply threat. Weekend Middle East coverage stayed diplomatic in tone, centred on Iran-Oman discussion of a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, with no new escalation showing market transmission. Friday's index internals were rotational rather than directional: semiconductors uniformly lower, with NVDA -4.57%, ARM -6.33%, AMD -2.33% and INTC -2.85%, against megacap gains in AMZN +3.97%, GOOGL +1.74%, MSFT +1.68% and AAPL +1.63%. Rotation of that kind normally reduces directional conviction rather than raising the probability of a persistent no-retracement path. Under the fixed mapping Tail 5 gives EA_ON and green. Stress is held at 26 to reflect an important repricing that no live tape has yet tested, and Confidence is 74, one point above the previous refresh, because the shared Finviz context file collected at 07:32 UTC is now inside its freshness window and independently corroborates the futures, breadth, megacap and semiconductor picture that was previously verified only through primary sources. That context is explicitly delayed, latest-session evidence and was not treated as live price-path evidence. Confidence stays bounded below the high band by the structural absence of any price path during the halt. A narrow observation window is flagged only across the 22:00 to 23:30 UTC reopen.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, spanning Friday's US cash session, the Friday settlement and the weekend halt. The series was uniformly green with Tail held at 5 and dominant mode normal throughout, while Stress sat in a 25-26 band. Confidence decayed from 77 to 58 as the published evidence aged across the closed weekend, then recovered to 64, 72 and 73 on the three most recent refreshes as sources were re-verified.
outlookSummary: The next 14 projected hours fall inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 26 to 29 as the reopen approaches and Confidence decays with ageing evidence. From the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen Tail is projected to lift to 12, still inside the low band, covering the first live test of near-coin-flip September rate-hike pricing, thin reopen liquidity and two-way gap risk. It then eases to 9-11 through the Asian session and into the European morning on expected volatility decay, while Confidence recovers because a live tape would exist again. Every post-reopen structure is stated conditionally because none of it is observable now. Monday 31 August brings month-end flows and a UK bank holiday that would conditionally thin the European handover, with Dallas Fed Manufacturing at 14:30 UTC the only scheduled US release that day. The data-heavy week beyond this horizon opens with ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September and runs to Nonfarm Payrolls on 4 September. The mapped policy state stays EA_ON across all 24 projected hours.
